::: {#def-marginal-likelihood}
#### Marginal likelihood

Given a prior $\p(\theta)$
and a model $\p(\vy \mid \theta)$ for the data given $\theta$,
the **marginal likelihood** (also called the **evidence**)
of observed data $\vy$ is

$$
\p(\vy) \eqdef \int \p(\vy \mid \theta)\, \p(\theta)\, d\theta,
$$

with the integral replaced by a sum over the possible values of $\theta$
when $\theta$ is discrete.
:::
